title: Oakshore Bank — Data Residency Discovery
summary: Discovery call focused on Oakshore's data residency and compliance requirements for Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments. Key concerns: GDPR/data locality, HIPAA-sensitive PII, banking regulatory controls, audit logs/retention, KMS/HSM integration, and restrictions on token logging. Redwood AE/SE covered deployment options, VPC/private control plane, encryption-at-rest/in-transit, and proposed next steps for security docs and an on-prem pilot runbook.

transcript:
Meeting header
Date/Time: 2026-04-20 15:00 EDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood, AE), Jillian Tran (Redwood, SE), Karen Miles (Oakshore, CISO), Tom Rivera (Oakshore, Head of Platform), Lena Ortiz (Oakshore, Director of Compliance)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect): Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment; data residency controls in EU/US; logging and token retention; KMS/HSM integration; SOC2 and financial services controls.

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir, AE at Redwood Inference. With me is Jillian, our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Karen: Doing good, thanks. Busy week but glad to be here.
[00:10] Tom: Morning all, thanks for setting this up.
[00:13] Samir: Cool, quick agenda: we'll run through your high-level compliance requirements, talk about deployment options (hosted, dedicated, private), cover encryption/KMS and logging, then Jillian will do a quick tech overview and we can capture next steps. Sound ok?
[00:22] Karen: Perfect. We're focused on two things: 1) data residency and GDPR — some workloads must stay in the EEA; 2) banking security requirements — audit logs, limited retention, and no retention of certain PII or raw input tokens for analytics.
[00:35] Jillian: Got it. Can you remind us which workloads you plan to push to inference? High-level is fine.
[00:40] Lena: Mainly customer support assistant, a secure document summarization for loan docs, and some internal knowledge search. The loan docs may contain customer identifiers and some health-related info occasionally — so HIPAA-ish concerns for certain fields.
[00:55] Samir: Thanks. Useful. So two big constraints: data residency (EEA-only for some models) and sensitive PII/HIPAA-like fields where logging must be carefully controlled. I'll hand to Jillian to describe how Redwood maps to hosted/dedicated/private for those concerns.
[01:06] Jillian: Sure. Quick high-level: Hosted is our standard public API — easiest to get started, global model catalog. For customers with strict residency and audit constraints we recommend Dedicated or Private. Dedicated is reserved capacity in our cloud region — you get dedicated GPUs and a logical isolation layer; data can be pinned to region but the control plane is still hosted by Redwood. Private is either VPC-connected private control plane or on-prem install where the control plane sits in your network, and that gives you the strongest data residency and audit control.
[01:40] Tom: When you say control plane hosted vs private, does that mean with Dedicated Redwood still sees any logs or tokens? We can't have raw tokens leave our environment for the loan doc flows.
[01:50] Jillian: With Dedicated we operate the control plane but you can configure logging to avoid storing raw prompts. We have options: minimal logs (only request metadata), mask PII at ingestion, or enable prefix/KV cache without persistent token logs. However, for ultimate assurance — especially where policy says data cannot leave our VPC — Private (VPC or on-prem) is the recommended route.
[02:15] Karen: Okay, what about KMS/HSM integration? We need to use our KMS for the keys and we require customer-managed keys for at-rest encryption.
[02:23] Jillian: We support customer-managed KMS in Dedicated via integration with AWS KMS or GCP KMS depending on region. For Private on-prem deployments, you can use an HSM and we can integrate with your PKCS#11-backed key management. For the hosted tier we use provider-managed keys; we can discuss Bring Your Own Key for certain enterprise contracts though it has caveats.
[02:45] Tom: How about audit logs and retention windows? Regulators want 7 years for some transaction traces, but we also have requirements to purge raw configurable PII within 30-90 days. Can Redwood satisfy both?
[02:58] Jillian: We can configure retention for different classes of logs. For audit traces you can keep metadata longer (7+ years) in an archival store — S3/GCS — and for raw prompts we offer redact-on-ingest and TTL-based deletion. On Private deployments you fully control retention since logs live in your environment. On Dedicated we provide configurable retention policies and an export pipeline to your storage for long-term retention.
[03:25] Karen: There's an internal prohibition on storing full transcripts or model inputs for certain loan types. Is there a way to disable token logging entirely for specific routes?
[03:33] Jillian: Yes, per-route logging policies are supported. You can set route-level policies: no-input-logs, no-output-logs, or masked logging. We also have automatic PII detection to redact common identifiers, but for banking IDs we'll want to validate the detection rules against your examples.
[03:52] Lena: Good — we'll share examples. Also, on GDPR, we need data to remain within the EEA for EU customers. Does Redwood Hosted guarantee region lock?
[04:02] Samir: Hosted is multi-region; we have EU regional endpoints but some backend services may still operate outside. For strict EEA lock-down, Dedicated pinned to an EU region or Private control plane in your EU VPC is the solution.
[04:18] Tom: Understood. A question on model variants: sometimes we fallback to smaller quantized models for cost. Are those considered a different transfer of data? We need to ensure that fallback doesn't route EU data to non-compliant regions or cloud accounts.
[04:30] Jillian: Great point. We enforce routing policies by region and model. For Dedicated/Private you can lock a profile to allowed model families and regions; automatic fallback to cheaper variants is controlled by policy — we can disable cross-region fallback and restrict to quantized variants within the same region/hardware pool.
[04:47] Karen: What's the auditing for who accessed what data? We need RBAC, SSO, and a full audit trail for keystroke-level ops?
[04:55] Jillian: We integrate with SAML/SSO for RBAC, and every API call is logged as an audit event with user context. For Private you can route audit logs to your SIEM. For Dedicated we can push logs to your logging endpoint or provide a log export. API-level audit is available including auth principal, route, model, and duration. We don't typically log keystroke-level detail unless you enable full transcript logging.
[05:20] Tom: Can you confirm encryption in transit? We need TLS mTLS for control plane comms and also for any agent communication.
[05:27] Jillian: Yes, we use TLS 1.2+ in transit and mTLS for Private control plane peering. Dedicated supports mutual TLS for data plane connections and we can provide cert rotation guidance.
[05:38] Karen: Any compliance attestations we can get quickly? SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001, PCI?
[05:44] Samir: We have SOC2 Type II and we're in the process of certifying ISO later this year. We don't process cardholder data directly but we have PCI- relevant controls; I will send the SOC2 report and our security pack after the call.
[05:58] Lena: For HIPAA, do you sign BAA? Some of our teams might ingest ePHI when customers include health history in docs.
[06:05] Samir: We do offer BAAs for customers that need them; it's typically part of our enterprise contract for Private or Dedicated deployments. We'll coordinate legal for that.
[06:13] Tom: Network-level question: for VPC peering or PrivateLink, what's required on our side? Firewall rules? Static IPs?
[06:20] Jillian: For VPC peering we need your VPC CIDR list and peering setup; Dedicated supports a set of static egress IPs for allow-listing. For PrivateLink we provide endpoints in your region. We'll send a network checklist that includes port lists, IP ranges to allow, and NAT/egress guidance.
[06:38] Karen: Any limitations on on-prem hardware for Private? GPU types, driver versions?
[06:43] Jillian: We publish a supported hardware matrix; generally we support NVIDIA A100/A30-class GPUs and specific driver/cuda versions. If your hardware is different we can evaluate. On-prem is more work but gives you full control.
[06:57] Tom: About logs again — regulators want immutable audit trails for certain actions. Is there WORM/append-only support for audit export?
[07:05] Jillian: For exported audit logs you can store them in WORM buckets on your side. Within Redwood we maintain immutable event logs for a configurable window; for longer-term immutability we'd suggest exporting to your archival store with WORM enabled.
[07:20] Karen: Are there any gotchas around tokenization or model caching — e.g., KV cache storing snippets that could persist beyond TTL? We want assurance caches don't leak PII.
[07:29] Jillian: We have KV cache lifecycle controls; caches can be per-session and TTL'd. On Dedicated/Private you can disable cross-session KV cache or ensure it never persists to disk. We'll provide the cache lifecycle docs and config flags.
[07:44] Lena: For the loan doc summarizer, we might pre-process data to mask identifiers client-side. Is Redwood ok with client-side redaction before sending?
[07:52] Samir: Absolutely — that's a recommended pattern. Client-side PII redaction reduces the compliance surface. We can also offer a hosted pre-processing step if needed.
[07:59] Tom: Any performance tradeoffs for disabling logs and caches? Our latency SLO is 200ms for short prompts in the support chat flow.
[08:08] Jillian: Minimal logging has negligible impact. Disabling KV cache pushes more load to tokens and can increase latency. For Dedicated with reserved GPUs you can meet 200ms SLOs for short prompts assuming right instance sizing and batching config. We'll propose a benchmarking run in the pilot.
[08:26] Karen: On the legal side, we'll need clarity on data processor vs controller responsibilities. Do you have standard language?
[08:33] Samir: We provide standard data processing addendum (DPA) language. For Private where control plane is in your network, responsibilities shift more to you; for Hosted/Dedicated we act as a processor with documented subprocessor lists. I'll include the DPA and subprocessor list in the doc pack.
[08:49] Lena: Great. A quick one: do you support region-restricted model fine-tuning or custom models that must never leave region?
[08:57] Jillian: Yes, with Dedicated/Private we can host model weights in-region and apply policies to prevent snapshot export. Fine-tuning workflows can be run in-region and the artifacts stored in your storage.
[09:09] Tom: On interop, we run on-prem databases and use internal auth. Can Redwood integrate with our SSO and LDAP for API keys rotations?
[09:18] Jillian: We integrate with SAML for SSO and can support SCIM for user provisioning. For API key rotation we support short-lived credentials and can integrate with your secrets manager for automated rotation in Private deployments.
[09:31] Karen: Ok that's helpful. To close, can we get a simple decision matrix: hosted vs dedicated vs private with compliance pros/cons?
[09:39] Samir: Sure. Hosted — fastest, lower cost, not guaranteed regional lock for all control plane services. Dedicated — reserved capacity, regional pinning, configurable logging and KMS but control plane still with Redwood. Private — most control: VPC/on-prem, customer-managed keys, full audit export; higher ops overhead and cost. I'll attach a one-pager.
[09:58] Tom: That will help. Also please include the network checklist and hardware matrix.
[10:03] Samir: Yep. Any other blockers?
[10:06] Lena: We'll need SOC2 + BAA confirmation and the DPA before legal kicks off.
[10:11] Samir: Understood, I'll send those.
[10:13] Karen: Alright, let's wrap. Thanks, this was productive.
[10:16] Samir: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and schedule Jillian's tech deep-dive.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription imperfections: some product names transcribed as "Redwood Dedicate" or "Redwood Priviate"; KV cache heard as "K V cash" in a few spots; occasional speaker label confusion where system tagged short interjections as "Speaker 3".

References shared during call: network checklist (link to be sent), SOC2 report (to be sent), security questionnaire (link), hardware matrix (link), DPA template (link).

Recap (short): Oakshore needs EEA region-lock for EU data, strict non-retention of certain PII and raw prompts, BAA for ePHI, customer-managed KMS for Dedicated/Private, per-route logging controls, and exportable immutable audit logs. Redwood proposed Dedicated or Private and will provide SOC2, DPA, network checklist, hardware matrix, and schedule a technical deep-dive and pilot scope meeting.
